mcq.q: What is printed by this pseudocode?
mcq.code:
SET a = 1, b = 1
REPEAT 5 TIMES
    SET t = a + b
    SET a = b
    SET b = t
END REPEAT
PRINT b

a=b=1
for _ in range(5):
    a, b = b, a+b
print(b)

mcq.q: What is printed by this pseudocode?
mcq.code:
FUNCTION f(n)
    IF n == 0 THEN RETURN 0
    RETURN (n MOD 10) + f(n DIV 10)
END FUNCTION
PRINT f(4096)

verify.src:
f=lambda n: 0 if n==0 else n%10+f(n//10)
print(f(4096))

mcq.q: Which of these is a checked exception in Java?
Which Java keyword prevents a method from being overridden?
Java is 'pass by value'. What does that mean when an object reference is passed to a method?
options: The reference is copied, so the method can mutate the object but cannot rebind the caller's variable
The caller's variable can be reassigned by the method
Objects cannot be modified inside methods
mcq.answer: The reference is copied, so the method can mutate the object but cannot rebind the caller's variable

mcq.q: In C++, why should a base class meant for polymorphic use have a virtual destructor?
options: So deleting a derived object through a base pointer runs the derived destructor
So the class cannot be instantiated
mcq.answer: So deleting a derived object through a base pointer runs the derived destructor

mcq.q: What is short-circuit evaluation?

Stopping a loop after one iteration
mcq.answer: Skipping the second operand of && / || when the first already decides the result

mcq.q: What is the average time complexity of checking membership (x in s) for a Python set?
What does it mean that JavaScript runs on a single thread with an event loop?
options: Code runs on one main thread; async callbacks are queued and run when the call stack is empty
Only one JavaScript file can be loaded per page

Promises execute in parallel on multiple cores
mcq.answer: Code runs on one main thread; async callbacks are queued and run when the call stack is empty

mcq.q: Which statement about recursion and iteration is true?
options: Any recursive algorithm can be rewritten iteratively using an explicit stack
Recursion is always faster than iteration
mcq.answer: Any recursive algorithm can be rewritten iteratively using an explicit stack

mcq.q: What is the difference between a compile-time error and a runtime error?
options: Compile-time errors are caught before the program runs; runtime errors happen during execution
Runtime errors are caught by the compiler
Compile-time errors only occur in interpreted languages
mcq.answer: Compile-time errors are caught before the program runs; runtime errors happen during execution
